title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a page of handwritten scratch notes in blue ink. It is written on the back of a reused typescript page. The faint typed text shows through: §13 of a chapter 'IX' on relative analytic groups and formal completion along a fibre. The neighbouring pages are typed pages 168–170 of that chapter, which has nothing to do with the handwriting.

**Opening sentence.** It ends a remark. Something (probably a category of morphisms or automorphisms of the objects under study) is 'équivalent à des groupoïdes connexes définis par deux groupes, que nous n'avons pas encore pu déterminer [dans le cas X = …]'. The final symbol is hard to read: possibly O_S, G_a or G_S. Read literally, the answer is a groupoid-type invariant described by a pair of groups (a π0/π1 or 2-group-like datum) that Grothendieck had not computed.

**The diagram.** It sets up a universal property of a completed divided-power (PD) de Rham complex.
- A_* is a (graded) k-module containing k, with a distinguished element T spanning k.
- B_* = A_*/k_*.
- The completed PD de Rham complex DR^(A^{10}_*, T) is identified with Γ^*(A_*) ⊗̂_k Λ^*(B_*): completed divided powers on A tensored with the exterior algebra on B = A/k. This is the standard shape Γ(M) ⊗ Λ(M) of the PD de Rham (Koszul-type) complex of a PD polynomial algebra, with the distinguished direction T modded out in the forms.
- This complex maps to a bigraded completed object Â^{**}_*. A morphism u: Â^{**} → Â'^{**} is to be induced by a dashed map v from DR^(A^{10}, T).

**Data defining v.** Grothendieck then lists the data needed to give such a map:
- a map v: A_* → A'^{**+} (positive total degree) with T ↦ T;
- its components v(p,q): A → A'^{pq} for p,q ≥ 0 and p+q > 0;
- normalised by v(1,0)(T) = T and v(p,q)(T) = 0 for (p,q) ≠ (1,0);
- so for (p,q) ≠ (1,0) the components factor through maps v̄(p,q): B = A/k → A'^{pq}.

The small square k ⊂ A, v(1,0) down to k ⊂ A'^{1,0}, records the compatibility with the inclusion of k. The last sketch, k ⊂ A → B → A'^{pq} together with Ω_* ⊗ A, starts describing the target components (A'^{pq} = …) but breaks off.

**Purpose.** In the context of cote 136 (PD de Rham complex, IHÉS lecture 1976), this looks like computing morphisms or automorphisms of the PD de Rham complex functor. Such a morphism is determined by where the generators go, subject to a normalisation on T. The groupoid remark then says the resulting automorphism/morphism groupoids are connected and governed by two groups not yet computed.
errors: No outright errors are visible. The page is fragmentary: the last formula 'A'^{pq} =' is left unfinished, and the identification DR^(A^{10},T) = Γ^*(A) ⊗̂ Λ^*(B) is stated without the differential.
The opening claim leaves the two groups explicitly undetermined.

ideas.what: The completed PD de Rham complex of a module with a distinguished element T, written as Γ^*(A) ⊗̂ Λ^*(A/k)
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power de Rham / Koszul complex of a PD polynomial algebra (PD Poincaré lemma setting)
ideas.where_published: Background in Berthelot, 'Cohomologie cristalline des schémas de caractéristique p>0' (LNM 407, 1974); the 1976 IHÉS lecture itself is not published as far as I know

ideas.what: Universal property: maps out of the completed PD de Rham complex into a bigraded algebra A'^{**} are given by components v(p,q): A → A'^{pq}, normalised by v(1,0)(T)=T and v(p,q)(T)=0 otherwise, hence factoring through B = A/k
ideas.modern_name: Universal property / endomorphisms of the de Rham complex functor (operations on de Rham cohomology)

ideas.what: Claim that the relevant category is equivalent to connected groupoids determined by two groups, which remain to be computed
ideas.modern_name: 2-group / groupoid of automorphisms of a functorial complex

missed.claim: Grothendieck states that some classification (likely of automorphisms or morphisms of the PD de Rham complex as a functor) reduces to connected groupoids described by two groups, which he had not yet determined in a basic case.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Automorphisms of the functorial de Rham / PD de Rham complex are of current interest: derived de Rham, the de Rham stack, and the 'symmetries' of de Rham cohomology studied by Drinfeld and Bhatt–Lurie. An explicit early question about such a two-group invariant could be compared with these computations. The connection is speculative given how fragmentary the page is.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is fragmentary working notes setting up a standard universal property of the completed PD de Rham complex. The only non-routine element is a one-line unresolved question about two groups classifying some groupoid, and its object is not identifiable with certainty.
transcription_corrections: First line: likely 'équivalent à des groupoïdes connexes', not 'équivalent de groupoïdes connexes'.
The arrow out of A_* is labelled v, and its target is written A'^{***+} (or A'^{**+}), meaning the positive-degree part.
Under Λ^*(B_*) it is written '= A_*/k_*', identifying B_* = A_*/k_*.
Middle diagram: the label on the dashed arrow is v (or v̄), and below DR^(A^{10}_*, T) there is '= (Â_*)'.
The last symbol in '[dans le cas X = …]' is unclear: possibly O_S, G_S or G_a.
